On a night where fine margins defined the outcome, AC Milan and Juventus battled to a frantic stalemate that was ultimately decided by the intervention of technology. The San Siro bore witness to a high-stakes tactical chess match on April 26, 2026, where a disallowed first-half strike served as the afternoon’s painful peak for the visitors. First Half: VAR Denies the Breakthrough The match began with both sides searching for rhythm, though the early exchanges were defined more by defensive discipline than offensive flair. Juventus looked to exert control through Jeremie Boga’s set-piece delivery, but his 11th-minute corner failed to find a teammate. The intensity boiled over in the 20th minute when Andrea Cambiaso earned the game’s first yellow card, setting a physical tone for the afternoon. The defining moment of the first half arrived in the 37th minute. Juventus believed they had snatched the lead when Khephren Thuram-Ulien found the back of the net, sparking wild celebrations in the away end. However, the joy was short-lived. Following a lengthy VAR review, the referee revoked the goal , ruling Thuram-Ulien offside by the narrowest of margins. The tension remained high as Milan’s Davide Bartesaghi was booked just a minute later, ensuring the sides went into the tunnel level. Second Half: Tactical Shuffles and Defensive Grit Returning for the second half , Milan manager opted for an immediate change, replacing the cautioned Bartesaghi with Pervis Estupinan. The home side struggled to test the Juventus keeper, with Christian Pulisic being withdrawn after an hour for the physical presence of Niclas Fuellkrug. As the clock ticked down, the sports spectacle became a battle of attrition. Juventus introduced Teun Koopmeiners and Emil Holm to inject fresh energy, while Milan turned to Christopher Nkunku in place of Rafael Leao. Despite the changes, clear-cut openings remained a rarity. Jeremie Boga and Estupinan both saw yellow as the play became increasingly fragmented by tactical fouls. Late Drama and Final Whistle The final ten minutes offered the most significant chance for a winner. In the 86th minute, Emil Holm delivered a pinpoint cross into the box, finding the head of Jonathan David. The striker, however, could only watch in frustration as his effort drifted agonizingly wide of the post. Shortly after, Manuel Locatelli was lucky to stay on the pitch after a reckless challenge on Adrien Rabiot resulted in a yellow card. In the dying embers of stoppage time, Juventus thought they had one final opening, but Dusan Vlahovic was caught in the offside trap in the 93rd minute. As the referee blew the final whistle at 90+7', the stats reflected the parity of the match , with Juventus edging possession at 52% to Milan’s 48%. For both giants, it was a night of what-might-have-been in the race for the Scudetto. Final Score: AC Milan 0-0 Juventus

The Serie A giants Juventus and Fiorentina faced off in a high-stakes encounter that tested the tactical discipline of both managers. The match, held on 2026-05-17 at the Allianz Stadium, offered a rollercoaster of emotions as the two historic rivals battled for supremacy on the pitch. Ndour Breaks the Deadlock The contest began with Juventus attempting to control the tempo through possession, yet Fiorentina remained structurally sound from the opening whistle. The breakthrough arrived in the 34th minute when Manor Solomon turned provider, setting up Cher Ndour . The young midfielder made no mistake, firing a right-footed shot home to give the visitors a crucial lead. Juventus struggled to find a clinical edge in response, with Gleison Bremer and Kenan Yildiz finding their efforts frustrated by a disciplined Viola backline. VAR Controversy and a Red Card The second half was defined by moments of high tension and officiating drama. In the 70th minute, the home crowd erupted as Dusan Vlahovic appeared to have leveled the score, but the joy was short-lived. Following a lengthy VAR intervention, the goal was chalked off for offside. The situation grew even more volatile just two minutes later when Luca Ranieri was shown a straight red card following heavy protests, forcing Fiorentina to defend their lead with only ten men for the remainder of the game. Mandragora Seals the Result Despite being a man down, the visitors remained a threat on the counter-attack as Juventus pushed forward in search of an equalizer. In the 83rd minute, substitute Rolando Mandragora produced a moment of magic, launching a spectacular left-footed strike from outside the box that flew past the goalkeeper. Although Juventus threw everything forward in stoppage time, including efforts from Fabio Miretti and headers from Bremer , the Fiorentina defense held firm to claim a famous victory on the road.

The Allianz Stadium played host to a tense Serie A encounter on May 3, 2026 , as two sides looked to secure vital points in the league standings. Both teams brought high intensity to the pitch, knowing that every tactical decision and individual moment of brilliance could define their season's trajectory. Lightning Start in Turin Juventus wasted no time establishing dominance, stunning their opponents with a goal in the opening minute of play. Andrea Cambiaso provided a pinpoint assist for Dusan Vlahovic , who clinicaly finished with his left foot to give the home side an immediate lead. The pressure continued to mount, and just four minutes later, Chico Conceicao came inches away from doubling the advantage, but his strike rattled the post and stayed out. The first half was characterized by Juventus controlling 65% of the ball and creating numerous opportunities. Gleison Bremer even attempted an audacious bicycle kick in the 22nd minute that flew wide, while Kenan Yildiz and Conceicao kept the Lecce defense busy with a series of dangerous corner deliveries. Despite the pressure, the visitors managed to stay within reach as the match progressed into a tactical battle. VAR Drama and Defensive Resilience The second half turned into a frustrating affair for the Bianconeri as they battled both the Lecce defense and the technology. Twice the stadium erupted as Juventus appeared to have found a second goal—first in the 49th minute and again in the 61st—only for VAR to intervene and rule both strikes out for offside. Dusan Vlahovic found himself frequently caught by the visitors' offside trap, leading to a stop-start rhythm that kept the result in the balance. As the clock ticked down, tactical substitutions saw Federico Gatti , Jonathan David , and Edon Zhegrova enter the fray to help see out the result. Lecce attempted to find an equalizer late on, with Lassana Coulibaly sending an effort wide, but Juventus remained composed. In the dying seconds, Wladimiro Falcone produced two vital saves to deny David and Zhegrova , ensuring that while the scoreline remained narrow, Juventus walked away with all three points.
